content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat cheddar is a semi‑hard cheese made from cow’s milk in which a portion of the cream is removed or replaced with skim milk. It retains the sharp, tangy flavor of traditional cheddar while providing fewer calories and less saturated fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheddar originated in the English village of Cheddar in the 12th century and is now one of the world’s most popular cheeses.
Fat reduction is achieved by separating part of the milk fat after curd formation.
The cheese is aged from 3 to 12 months; longer aging intensifies the flavor.
Reduced‑fat cheddar is favored in diet‑focused meals where cheese texture is desired without the full calorie load.
It melts well, making it a common choice for sauces, casseroles, and pizza.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Provides about 700 mg of calcium per 100 g, supporting bone and teeth health.

items.title: Good source of protein
items.content: Delivers roughly 25 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 aids nerve function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Lower saturated fat
items.content: Reduced fat content makes it more suitable for diets limiting saturated fats.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Like other fermented cheeses, cheddar contains live cultures that can benefit gut microbiota.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: The cheese still contains lactose; individuals with intolerance should limit intake.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Some people may react to casein, the main milk protein.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheddar can be salty; those with hypertension should monitor portion size.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite reduced fat, it remains calorie‑dense; moderation is key.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Reduced‑fat cheddar works well sliced for sandwiches, cubed in salads, grated for sauces, casseroles, and pizza. It can also be enjoyed as a snack on its own.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in its original packaging or an airtight container in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. It stays fresh for up to 4 weeks. If mold appears, cut away the affected area and use the remaining cheese.
